correctness.rationale: For a correct voters and b incorrect voters, additive epsilon least core permits signed efficient x. The a correct singleton constraints and the all-incorrect coalition force epsilon >= (a-v(N))/(a+1); when a>=b+2, averaging winning coalitions consisting of b+1 correct plus all incorrect gives epsilon >= (a-b-1)/(a-b). Explicit type-symmetric p,q attain their maximum, and proper tie coalition small edge cases (1,1),(2,1) are checked. Homogeneous all-correct and all-incorrect cases use singleton averaging/zero allocation. Independently solved unrestricted individual-variable LPs for 27 mixed and homogeneous profiles with 2<=n<=7; matches six exact branches, but finite LP does not prove general case.

originality.rationale: The precise binary random-tie plurality accuracy game is already defined by Sarpe–Georgakopoulos–Gionis; their Banzhaf and Shapley allocations do not solve the least-core minimax coalition problem. General least-core LP duality solves arbitrary finite instances but does not imply a closed parametric formula or its sharp transition a=2b+1. Indexed related voting-power results are distinct ranking/attribution questions. Best-of-knowledge originality is confined to the all-(a,b) exact deficit and optimizer with signed transfers.
